column2: Add the spices, salt, baking powder and flour and mix; rest in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Shape walnut-sized balls, press lightly and place on the tray; brush with the remaining oil.
Bake for 12 minutes, turn and bake 10–12 minutes more until both sides are golden.
Use soaked raw chickpeas, not cooked ones; cooked chickpeas make the mixture fall apart.
Contains much less oil than frying.
Serve with tahini-yoghurt sauce, salad and wholemeal lavash.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat in the oven.
Yoghurt chia pudding
3 tablespoons chia seeds
A handful of seasonal fruit
1 tablespoon roughly chopped walnuts
Mix the chia, milk, yoghurt and honey well in a bowl.
Stir again after 5 minutes to prevent lumps.
Cover and leave in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Divide the pudding between bowls and top with fruit and walnuts.
Make it the evening before and eat it at breakfast.
Oats with tahini and grape molasses
1 teaspoon grape molasses (pekmez)
Put the oats and milk in a small pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5–6 minutes until thickened.
Transfer to a bowl and stir in the cinnamon.
Slice the banana and arrange on top.
Drizzle with the tahini and molasses and serve.
Tahini and molasses contain iron and calcium; a good breakfast choice.
Add a little more milk if you prefer it runnier.
Scrambled eggs with chard
Wash the chard well; chop the stalks finely and the leaves roughly.
Chop the onion finely and fry it in the olive oil for 3 minutes.
Add the chard stalks and cook for 2 minutes, then add the leaves and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Crack in the eggs and mix with the salt and chilli flakes.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the eggs are completely set.
You can use spinach instead of chard.
Cook until no runny egg remains.
Serve hot; yoghurt goes well alongside.
Baked courgette flowers stuffed with cheese
3 sprigs of mint
Preheat the oven to 190°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Gently remove the pistil from inside each courgette flower; rinse quickly under running water and drain.
Mix the curd cheese, crumbled white cheese, chopped dill, mint and the egg.
Put a dessertspoon of filling in each flower and twist the tips to close.
Arrange on the tray and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until the filling is cooked and the flowers are lightly golden.
Courgette flowers are very delicate; use fresh flowers picked that morning.
Don’t overfill; the filling spills out during baking.
Spinach and cheese gözleme
2 tablespoons butter (for the top)
Knead the flour, salt, olive oil and water into a soft dough; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Wash and finely chop the spinach; squeeze out the excess water.
Finely chop the onion and mix with the spinach and crumbled cheese.
Divide the dough into 4 and roll each piece thinly on a floured surface.
Spread filling over one half, fold the other half over and press the edges to seal.
Cook on a hot griddle or in a wide pan for 3–4 minutes per side, until brown spots appear.
Brush with butter, slice and serve.
If you don’t squeeze the spinach well, the dough stays soggy.
The thinner you roll the dough, the better the gözleme.
Serve hot with ayran.
Eat fresh; reheat leftovers in a pan.
Eggs in tomato and pepper sauce (shakshuka)
Finely chop the onion and peppers, grate the tomatoes and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion and peppers for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 8–10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make 4 wells in the sauce with a spoon and crack in the eggs.
Cook covered for 6–8 minutes until both whites and yolks are fully set.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.
